findings.reason: The first implementation called list(records) and list(source_observations) before checking limits, so an unbounded generator could be fully consumed. The approval was extended with max_sources and source_limit_exceeded; focused regressions observed the old whole-generator consumption, then passed after bounded consumption through limit plus one.

The first implementation treated a source identity repeated by two different records as a duplicate source ref. A focused regression failed with that error; the fix now permits shared source observations while still counting every record ref and refusing duplicate observations.

A refused report included the original input index, so reordering malformed records changed the report bytes. A focused regression failed; inputs are now sorted by their canonical value before diagnostic indexes are assigned and findings are sorted by typed code and index.

Malformed records and observations initially raised immediately rather than producing a bounded refused report. Focused regressions now require stable typed findings without raw content, and the implementation returns a canonical refused envelope while only unsafe envelope/limit conditions raise MemoryDoctorError.

The second review found that max_findings rejected otherwise well-formed evidence with more findings than the retention bound, and non-iterable inputs reused limit error types. Regressions now require a stable retained prefix plus omitted_findings, distinct invalid_records/invalid_source_observations errors, and a six-thousand-observation bound probe; all pass after the fix.

The fifth bounded pass added focused evidence for canonically equivalent-but-distinct Unicode memory IDs and for retaining a typed contradiction when unrelated findings precede it. Both passed without production-code changes; they close coverage gaps rather than alter the frozen contract.
This session performed the contract, source, test and diff review, but did not dispatch an independent fresh-context reviewer. Landing must not claim independent review from this author-side record.
